title: Update ERC-8226: Scope mandates by target with actions and limits (ethereum/ERCs PR #2191)
notes: gh api repos/ethereum/ERCs/pulls/2191 on 2026-11-21: opened 2026-11-20T10:52:29Z by thamerdridi (Thamer Dridi, Brickken), merged 2026-11-20T11:14:10Z by eip-review-bot, merge commit 9912307 (99123078478fb56b1b5a5abcbb6b6207dba70832), 17 files, +1,801 -1,051. Text read with git show 9912307:ERCS/erc-8226.md (750 lines) in research/vendor/ERCs and compared with 9912307^, the text of PR #2060 (commit f4df3d0, 2026-10-09). Status still Draft and description unchanged (a compliance delegation layer for AI agents operating on tokenized regulated assets). New: mandates keyed by (agent, principal, target), the target being the contract the agent calls, instead of (agent, principal, asset); the scope is a list of actions (bytes32 labels, each with calldata constraints: index, check EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, AT_MOST or AT_LEAST, value; several EQUALS constraints on one index form an allowlist) plus limits per asset and direction (OUTFLOW or INFLOW) with maxTransactionValue, maxCumulativeValue and cumulativeUsed, shared by all the mandate's actions; canExecute and recordExecution take (agent, principal, target, action, data, flows), a flow being (asset, direction, amount); a non-zero flow with no matching limit fails with NO_LIMIT; new reasons CONSTRAINT_FAILED and NO_LIMIT; recordExecution reverts with MandateBlocked(reason); a new grant clears the prior actions and limits, and the signer sets each limit's starting cumulativeUsed; an approved operator may grant, revoke and extend mandates, directly or by signature, but may not set operators; only the principal approves operators, and an enforcer may call setOperator only to remove one; enforcers freeze and cannot revoke; ERC-165 ids IAgentMandate 0x5aa4c7e4 and IComplianceProvider 0xfa2a39b3; RAMS now defines three interfaces, IAgentExecutor OPTIONAL. Already in the 2026-10-09 text: the three enforcement venues (token gate, EIP-7702 account, executor) and IAgentExecutor as an OPTIONAL, non-normative companion interface, and operators could already revoke and extend. Moved or changed: IAgentExecutor into the Specification; the account venue as one stateless EIP-7702 delegate code deployment per chain and registry, or a module such as a Safe module (which needs the recorder role); a standalone executor for EVM chains without EIP-7702 that MUST serve one principal; executors SHOULD measure the principal's balance changes around each call. The text still names ERC-8004 as an example identity layer and does not mention AP2, x402 or any card network.

title: Update ERC-8048: Make agent profile keys onchain only (ethereum/ERCs PR #2181)
notes: gh api on 2026-11-21: by nxt3d (Prem Makeig), opened 2026-11-17T04:44:01Z, merged 2026-11-17T04:53:06Z, commit f9091bc. Text read with git show f9091bc:ERCS/erc-8048.md: ERC-8048 'Onchain Metadata for Token Registries', Draft, created 2025-09-30, authors Prem Makeig and Rafael Abuawad, requires 165, 7930 and 8119. Its Agent Metadata Profile (nicknamed ERC-721T) reserves per-token keys for ERC-721 tokens that represent agents: context; endpoint[<type>] with mcp, a2a, web (aligned with ERC-8004's web service usage), x402 and ens; address[<chain-id>], keyed by the ERC-7930 Chain Identifier; and the optional account[<chain-id>][<index>]. They are read with metadata(uint256,string) and change with the MetadataSet event. New in f9091bc: the profile keys MUST be stored on-chain, on the token contract or a metadata_contract sidecar, and MUST NOT appear in tokenURI or uri JSON; clients MUST read them with metadata(uint256,string) and MUST ignore JSON members with these names; the stated reason is that JSON can change without a MetadataSet event while clients act on these values, for example by sending funds to address[<chain-id>]. The profile predates the change (present at b1f2bd8, 2026-10-10). title: fix: bind ERC-8004 verification to a trusted origin (wevm/mppx PR #1332)
notes: gh api on 2026-11-21: opened 2026-11-19T16:09:05Z by brendanjryan, state open, not merged (last updated 2026-11-19T16:26:25Z). It would add an optional origin setting to the ERC-8004 server configuration and reject mismatches before the registry lookup. Its motivation says a relayed ERC-8004 signature can authenticate at another service when the request URL is derived from an attacker-controlled Host; that is the author's statement, not a security advisory. Separately, PR #1327 (merged 2026-11-18) added optional exact host allowlists to the Express and Node adapters, released in mppx 0.21.0 (npm 2026-11-19T02:08:47Z).
